name: Atmospheric CO₂
summary: CO₂ 429.02 ppm at Mauna Loa in the week of 15 Nov, up 2.18 ppm on a year, inside the 2–3 ppm Watch band
state: Mauna Loa recorded 429.02 ppm in the week of 15 Nov, 2.18 ppm higher than a year earlier and inside the 2.0–3.0 ppm Watch band (NOAA GML). No newer weekly value was available on 24 Nov, and weekly growth figures are noisy. El Niño years tend to bring faster CO₂ growth as tropical land absorbs less carbon.
for_you: CO₂ growth is a slow-moving indicator of long-term warming rather than a near-term hazard.
rubric_hit: CO₂ +2.18 ppm y/y within 2.0–3.0 Watch band

sources.title: NOAA GML — Trends in atmospheric CO₂ (Mauna Loa)

why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.
